visuals.title: From the machine up to the human

stages.name: Machine language
stages.detail: 0s and 1s. Fastest, hardest to write, different for each machine.

stages.name: Assembly language
stages.detail: Short codes (mnemonics) like MOV and ADD. Fast but still hard and machine-dependent.

stages.name: Middle level: C, C++
stages.detail: High-level features such as functions, plus low-level access to memory. Powerful and fast, but needs care.

stages.name: High level: Python, Java, C#
stages.detail: Easy to read and write, machine-independent, but usually slower.

goal: After this you can explain what programming is, name the levels of programming languages with examples, and give reasons why C++ is called a middle-level language.
warmup: A recipe tells a cook what to do: ingredients (input), steps (processing) and the final dish (output). If a step is missing or in the wrong order, the dish fails. A program is a recipe for a computer. But a computer is like a cook who cannot think: it does exactly what the recipe says, even if the recipe is wrong.
definition: A computer follows instructions very fast but cannot think on its own. A program is a complete set of step-by-step instructions. Programming is the activity of writing those instructions, and the person who does it is a programmer. A programming language is a formal language with fixed rules (syntax) used to write the instructions. Languages are grouped by how close they are to the hardware (low level) or to humans (high level).
howItWorks: Almost every program follows the IPO model: Input (data given), Processing (calculation or decisions), Output (result shown). Languages come in levels. Low-level languages are close to the machine: machine language (only 0s and 1s) and assembly (short codes like MOV, ADD). They are fast but hard to write and work only on one kind of machine. High-level languages like Python, Java and C# look like English and run on many machines, but are usually slower. C and C++ are called middle level because they have high-level features (functions, classes, readable syntax) and also low-level features such as pointers and direct memory control. Levels exist because humans find words easy and machines find 0s and 1s easy, so we choose between ease and control. A translator (next lesson) converts our code into machine language. Many books simply call C++ high level; both answers appear in exams, so remember the reason behind each.

variations.when: Low level, short codes called mnemonics
variations.example: MOV AL, 61h   or   ADD A, B

variations.when: Middle level: readable but with memory control (pointers)
High level: easy, machine-independent, usually slower

mistakes.error: 'print' was not declared in this scope (print is Python, C++ uses cout)
'x' was not declared in this scope

mistakes.wrong: Saying: Assembly is easy to read, or C++ is only low level
mistakes.right: Assembly is low level and hard to read. C++ is middle level (many books say high level).
mistakes.error: Not a compiler error. This is a common wrong exam answer.

examTips: Define: program, programming, programmer, programming language.
Every program follows IPO: Input, Processing, Output.
Low level: machine language and assembly. Middle level: C and C++. High level: Python, Java, C#, BASIC.
Why C++ is middle level: it has high-level features (functions, classes) and low-level features (pointers, memory control).
Low level = fast, hard, machine-dependent. High level = easy, machine-independent, slower.
romanSummary: Program instructions ka set hai jo computer ko step-by-step batata hai. Computer khud nahi sochta.
Har program Input, Processing, Output (IPO) follow karta hai.
Low level language (machine, assembly) machine ke qareeb hoti hai: fast lekin mushkil aur machine-dependent.
High level language (Python, Java) insaan ke qareeb hai: asaan lekin thori slow. C/C++ middle level hain.

practice.hint: Data in, work done, result out.
practice.explanation: IPO is the model almost every program follows.
Machine language is binary. Assembly uses short codes like MOV and ADD.

practice.prompt: Fill in the blank: Python and Java are ______ level languages.
practice.hint: They look close to human language.
practice.explanation: High-level languages are easy to read and machine-independent.

practice.prompt: Why is C++ called a middle-level language?
options: It has high-level features and also low-level memory control
practice.answer: It has high-level features and also low-level memory control
practice.explanation: C++ combines readable features (functions, classes) with low-level control (pointers).
cout prints the label, then the value 150. No endl, so no new line.

practice.prompt:
Fix the bug (this is a Python habit):

print("Hello");
practice.hint: C++ uses a different output tool.
practice.explanation: In C++ you print with cout and <<. print is not the C++ way.

practice.prompt: Write a program that stores the number 5 in a, the number 3 in b, and prints a * b.
practice.hint: Declare two int boxes, then multiply.

practice.prompt: Which is a disadvantage of low-level languages?
practice.hint: They are close to the machine, not to humans.
practice.explanation: Low level gives speed but is hard to write and works only on one kind of machine.

quiz.prompt: A person who writes programs is called a:
quiz.hint: Programming is the activity, this is the person.
quiz.explanation: A programmer writes instructions for the computer.

quiz.prompt: Which of these is an example of a high-level language?
quiz.explanation: Python, Java, C# and BASIC are high level.

quiz.prompt: MOV AL, 61h is an example of:
quiz.explanation: MOV and ADD are mnemonics used in assembly.

quiz.prompt: What is one advantage of high-level languages?
quiz.hint: They are close to human language.
quiz.explanation: High level is easy to read and machine-independent, though usually slower.

quiz.prompt: Which feature makes C++ close to the machine?
quiz.hint: Direct memory handling is a low-level feature.
quiz.explanation: Pointers and direct memory management give C++ its low-level side.
